newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Trio of techs highlight options.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Trio of techs highlight options.

text.p: A trio of technology stock options highlighted activity on Monday, traders said.

Options on shares of Compaq Computer Corp were busy as the stock continued to rally after the company announced a stock split, and implied volatilities in CompuServe Corp and Motorola Inc were moving higher.

In late trading, Compaq shares were up 4-7/16 at 113-05/16 despite a broad market selloff. Last Tuesday, the computer maker announced a five-for-two stock split payable to shareholders of record July 14.
Mike Ditzler, pit representative in the Compaq options trading crowd at the Pacific Exchange, said investors were mainly buying calls.
"People are just buying up the calls," he said. "Mostly because of the stock split, but the whole market's been up the last couple of days so we've been up with it."
The bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI had climbed 223 points in the last three sessions. It extended gains early Monday before backing off in the afternoon.
Ditzler said outside of the call buying, activity in the Compaq options was fairly mixed.
"There's some trading going on but nothing big one way or the other," he said.
Among the Compaq options, the July 115 calls traded 4,845 contracts, the July 110 calls traded 3,715 and the July 105 calls traded nearly 3,700.
The most active puts were the July 100 and 105s, which traded 1,125 and 1,555 contracts, respectively.
CompuServe shares were up 1-5/16 at 12-1/16 in late trading on buyout speculation, traders said.
The Wall Street Journal said Monday that New York investment firm Welsh, Carson, Anderson & Stowe had joined other firms including America Online Inc in vying for CompuServe.
H&R Block is trying to sell its 80 percent stake in the on-line service and is holding out for better offers, the Journal said.

Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners at the American Stock Exchange said implied volatility in the busy August 12-1/2 calls on CompuServe had risen to the 75 area from the low to mid-60s.
"We're seeing a lot of retail call buying, specifically in the Aug 12-1/2 line," Schwarz said.
The CompuServe August 12-1/2 calls were the most active CompuServe option, with turnover of 525 contracts. The August 12-1/2 put traded 360.

In other trading, volatilities in Motorola options had reached the mid-40 region, up about 10 points over the last several sessions, ahead of the company's second quarter earnings, expected Tuesday, Schwarz said.
"It's not rampant speculation," he said, referring to earnings expectations. "There's nothing crazy going on."
Analysts' consensus estimate for Motorola's second quarter profits is $0.56 a share according to First Call.
